title: I found the spreadsheet where my parents tracked my rent. My brother paid nothing.
hook: I paid my parents six hundred a month for four years. Last week I found the spreadsheet. My brother's column said zero.
narration: I paid my parents six hundred a month for four years. Last week I found the spreadsheet. My brother's column said zero. Four years. Forty-eight months. Twenty-eight thousand eight hundred dollars, in my column, in my dad's handwriting. In my brother's, a row of zeros and one note: still studying. He finished studying two years ago. I didn't say anything at dinner. I just watched my mum pass him the last of the potatoes like she always does. Then I went back to the laptop, because the file had a third tab I'd skipped. It was called return. One line. My name, the full amount, and a date. Next month. The day after I told them I'd found a flat I couldn't quite afford. So. Do I ask them about the zero, or pretend I never saw it?
verdict: Ask. Gratitude and a question can share a sentence.
